sources.note: Only phonological description known for the Gira-Neko-Nekgini cluster; Nekgini is c. 70% lexically similar to Neko and Claassen & McElhanon (1970) / McElhanon (1975) suggest the two may be dialects of one language. An OPD normally has a 'stress' paragraph; would be the nearest proxy statement (identity caveat: nekg1240, not neko1240).

tone.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress does not seem to be phonemic. Tone is not found. All the vowels have lengthened counterparts, but context determines whether the vowel is long or short so length does not need to be written.
tone.locator: p.2, section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', immediately before 'Syllable Patterns'
tone.says: First-hand OPD statement for the closest related variety: under 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' it states that stress does not seem to be phonemic, that tone is not found, and that vowel length is contextually determined and not. No tone marking anywhere in the inventory, examples or sample text.
